title: Universal Printer Application Ladder — Mark / Luke / Interplanetary Infrastructure

use_case_families.reason: maximizes recursive manufacturing capacity before consuming capacity on end products

use_case_families.reason: turns heterogeneous local material into bounded printer feed

use_case_families.evidence_anchor: NASA current lunar ISRU work demonstrates integrated production of silicon solar cells, aluminum wire, oxygen, iron and slag from regolith simulant in lunar-like conditions

use_case_families.geometry_note: many RF/sensor functions change primarily through geometry/topology once conductor/dielectric/active interface primitives exist

use_case_families.cross_domain: same structural/power/sensing/control primitives apply on Earth, Moon and Mars with different environment/material envelopes

applications: mission-specific kinetic-deflection spacecraft structures/support hardware where independently designed and authorized

expansion_logic: printer capability grows by closing primitive-function and resource-feed gaps; end-use diversity comes from recombination rather than building a separate manufacturing stack for each application
